items.title: John L. Jones Interview, 1972-06-05
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...His full name. Did you know? And he had a, no I forgot, but I could get it. I'd love to know his right name. Everybody says he would.

ctx.x: Well, I was born in Donisonville, Louisiana on December 12, 1910. And I started music at about six years old. Started on the piano, my mother started teaching me rudiments on the piano. But I didn't like the piano. And I put the piano down and I got a ukulele. And I started in the country on the ukulele. Then by 1925 I came to New Orleans. Then I played the ukulele on the shoeshine stands and around the streets of New Orleans for years. And then I got a banjo. And I started taking the banjo from lessons from…
Yeah, but I never did know his right name. His full name. Did you know? And he had a, no I forgot, but I could get it. I'd love to know his right name. Everybody says he would.

And he had a drummer by the name of Albert Jow. You heard of him? Oh yeah. I knew him. Then we had all the way through, we had uh, uh, Poirier, Allison Poirier on piano. He stayed with Isaiah Morgan. And when I left Morgan, I joined the John Casimir band. The John Casimir, I started playing at Claiborne and Tulane Avenue. John had a man playing trumpet, he alternated by the name of Wooden Joe. Oh yeah. Uh huh. And that's who else John had. John had, I can't, I don't know the rest of this man's name. He had…
